value.detail: California is a mandatory state: 18 U.S.C. § 1162(a) (criminal) and 28 U.S.C. § 1360(a) (civil) extend state jurisdiction to all Indian country within California. log.limits: Indian Child Welfare Act: the 2026 notice (91 FR 30665) prints its table only as page images; the tribe column was read visually from the govinfo PDF rendered at 80 dpi, and names were matched to the roster (all 575 roster nations appear). Reading errors are possible for individual names; the July 2025 notice (90 FR 30950) has a text table and can be used to cross-check. Public Law 280: only nations whose BIA directory office state, or whose official name, places them in a mandatory state were marked mandatory-state, so lands of a nation in a second state may be missed. Optional-state was recorded only for Florida, Idaho, Iowa (Sac and Fox, civil only), Montana (Flathead) and Washington, where a current state statute could be cited; Arizona (air and water pollution only), Nevada (non-retroceded areas), North Dakota, South Dakota and Utah were left empty because no current nation-level source was found or the assumption depended on tribal consent that was never given. Pre-1994 retrocession notices are not full-text searchable in the Federal Register API; the 1969-1989 notices recorded were found from citations in a 2016 Office of Tribal Justice compilation and the Bois Forte notice from prior knowledge, then each was opened on govinfo. Other pre-1994 retrocessions may exist. Indian Child Welfare Act reassumption notices before 1994 were likewise not searchable (only Lac Courte Oreilles 1981 was found). Violence Against Women Act: the only public list of implementing nations found (NCAI) was last updated May 2022 (31 nations); many nations have begun exercising special Tribal criminal jurisdiction since the 2022 reauthorization, so this field is incomplete. Department of Justice pages give only the five pilot nations. Tribal Law and Order Act: no current published list was found; the 2015 Bureau of Justice Assistance publication (interviews from 2013) and three NCAI profile statements are the only sources, so coverage is far from complete. The archived NCAI list (tloa.ncai.org/tribesexercisingTLOA.cfm) is in the Wayback Machine but web.archive.org was blocked for this session. Memberships: Affiliated Tribes of Northwest Indians has no public member list on its site; Coalition of Large Tribes publishes only a partial list; Tanana Chiefs Conference, Bristol Bay Native Association and Kawerak list communities or councils without calling them members, so they were not recorded; Inter Tribal Council of Michigan, Maniilaq Association, Kodiak Area Native Association and California Rural Indian Health Board blocked requests; Eight Northern Indian Pueblos Council had no list. The Great Plains Tribal Chairmen's Association site returned no content. Piikani Nation (Canada), Trenton Indian Service Area and He Sapa area appear on member lists but are not roster nations and were not added as entities. Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians does not appear on the current United South and Eastern Tribes list as read.
log.narrative: Task A: statute text for 18 U.S.C. 1162 and 28 U.S.C. 1360 from Cornell's Legal Information Institute; mandatory-state facts generated from those statutes for nations whose office state is Alaska, California, Minnesota, Nebraska, Oregon or Wisconsin (or whose official name includes one), with Red Lake, Warm Springs and Metlakatla (criminal only) recorded as excepted and fully retroceded nations (Menominee, Burns Paiute, Santee Sioux) given only a retroceded fact. The Federal Register API returned the post-1994 retrocession notices (Salish and Kootenai, Tulalip, Santee Sioux, Yakama, Skokomish) and 18 U.S.C. 1162(d) concurrent federal jurisdiction grants (Mille Lacs, Hoopa Valley); older notices were opened through govinfo's citation link service and read in the OCR layer. Optional-state facts cite the state statutes themselves. The ICWA designated-agent list is the May 26, 2026 notice. VAWA and TLOA facts come from NCAI and Department of Justice pages. Task B: member lists were read directly from each organization's site (curl, WordPress REST API where the page was script-built, WebFetch for USET), then matched to roster ids with a normalizing matcher plus manual overrides; every non-literal match was reviewed by hand and flagged in the note with medium confidence. Constituent bands or communities listed separately (Minnesota Chippewa Tribe bands, Te-Moak bands, Washoe communities, Passamaquoddy reservations) were attributed to the roster nation and noted.
